title: Computational earthquake hazards
blurb: A progression from rupture physics and fault geometry to finite-element deformation, wave simulation, and probabilistic hazard.

person.name: Brad T. Aagaard
person.affiliation: U.S. Geological Survey, Earthquake Hazards Program
person.expertise: Earthquake source physics, ground-motion modeling, crustal characterization, and computational seismic hazard

papers.title: Seismology: Earthquake Rupture Dynamics: Comparing the Numerical Simulation Methods

notes.takeaway: Compares numerical approaches for dynamic rupture simulation.

papers.title: A Nitsche-extended finite element method for earthquake rupture on complex fault systems

notes.takeaway: Extended finite elements represent discontinuities on complex fault systems.
notes.why: Fault geometry is a numerical problem as well as a geological one.

papers.title: Observed source parameters for dynamic rupture with non-uniform initial stress and relatively high fracture energy

notes.takeaway: Relates stress drop, fracture energy, and rupture observations.
notes.why: Source parameters control the resulting wavefield.

papers.title: Inversion for the physical parameters that control the source dynamics of the 2004 Parkfield earthquake

notes.takeaway: Uses dynamic inversion to estimate rupture geometry, stress, and friction.
notes.why: Turns observed motion into physical source constraints.

papers.title: Variability of seismic source spectra, estimated stress drop, and radiated energy, derived from cohesive-zone models of symmetrical and asymmetrical circular and elliptical ruptures

notes.takeaway: Tests how rupture geometry and cohesive-zone assumptions affect spectra and radiated energy.

papers.title: Dynamic earthquake rupture simulations on nonplanar faults embedded in 3D geometrically complex, heterogeneous elastic solids

notes.takeaway: Simulates rupture on nonplanar faults in heterogeneous 3-D solids.
notes.why: Approaches the structural complexity hazard models need.

papers.title: A domain decomposition approach to implementing fault slip in finite-element models of quasi-static and dynamic crustal deformation

notes.takeaway: Uses domain decomposition and Lagrange multipliers to implement fault slip in PyLith.
notes.why: Aagaard contribution to reusable crustal modeling.

papers.title: CyberShake: A Physics-Based Seismic Hazard Model for Southern California

notes.takeaway: Builds probabilistic hazard from simulated ruptures and 3-D wave propagation.
notes.why: Canonical bridge from simulation to hazard curves.

papers.title: Hybrid broadband ground motion simulation validation of small magnitude earthquakes in Canterbury, New Zealand

notes.takeaway: Tests hybrid broadband simulations against observed motions.
notes.why: Validation turns plausible simulation into evidence.

papers.title: Findings from a decade of ground motion simulation validation research and a path forward

notes.takeaway: Synthesizes lessons from a decade of simulation-validation studies.
notes.why: Identifies evaluation gaps for operational use.

papers.title: Validation of earthquake ground-motion models in southern California, USA, using precariously balanced rocks

notes.takeaway: Uses precariously balanced rocks as evidence of past shaking beyond the instrumental record.
notes.why: Independent geological constraints test hazard tails.

papers.title: Evaluation and Updates for the USGS San Francisco Bay Region 3D Seismic Velocity Model in the East and North Bay Portions

notes.takeaway: Updates a regional 3-D velocity model used for ground-motion work.

sections.label: Foundations: rupture and fault geometry
sections.summary: The field begins by representing discontinuities, stress, friction, and geometry well enough for rupture to propagate. Numerical comparisons establish which approximations can move into larger simulations.

sections.label: Simulation: source to wavefield
sections.summary: Dynamic rupture models move from idealized faults to nonplanar interfaces in heterogeneous solids. Finite-element infrastructure makes deformation experiments reusable across regional problems.
questions: How should source and wave solvers exchange uncertainty?

sections.label: Hazard: ensembles and validation
sections.summary: Physics-based systems run rupture and wave scenarios, then compare outputs with recordings and geological constraints. The goal is calibrated decision support, not visual realism alone.

sections.label: Frontier: regional, open hazard models
sections.summary: Updated velocity models and shared validation connect computational geophysics to operational hazard assessment. The next step is provenance from fault assumptions through site-specific outputs.
questions: What inputs must every result publish?

opportunities: Pair source, velocity-model, and site uncertainties in shared regional test cases.
Design metrics honest where large earthquakes have no recordings.
practices: Compare simulations to waveforms, intensity measures, and geological constraints.

podcast.title: The computational earthquake
podcast.description: From fault mechanics through 3-D ground-motion simulation to useful hazard forecasts.
